text:
alex: Heads up — planning a terraform apply to prod for routing + IAM changes tonight at 22:05 UTC. 30m change window.

deploy-bot: :rocket: tf-apply scheduled by alex for 2026-03-20T22:05Z. run_id=tf-apply-20260320-01. targets=module.network, module.iam. Canary=10%. Auto-fallback enabled.

mira: listing version pins? want to avoid provider drift during apply.

alex: pinning provider aws to 4.63.1 and module/network to v2.4.0. updating release notes -> https://redwood.internal/releases/2026-03-20-routing-iam (public link in workspace).

samir: preflight checks? tfsec / terratest?

ops-bot: preflight results: tfsec=pass, terratest=partial (route53 test flaky), plan-size=48 resources, risky_changes=3 (route replacements).

alex: route replacements are deliberate (split CIDR & new TG health-checks). we ran terratest locally, flaky check is noise.

kyle: quick ask — what are circuit-breaker thresholds? when does deploy-bot auto-abort?

deploy-bot: auto-abort conditions: >5% 5m error-rate on canary OR any control-plane API 500s during apply OR resource_create_failures >2. will pause and notify channel.

ivy: adding rollback playbook steps here so on-call can act fast:
1) pause canary and stop traffic shift (deploy-bot pause).
2) revert to tag network@v2.3.8 and iam@v1.9.2 (git revert + push).
3) run terraform apply -target=module.network -var-file=rollback.tfvars in emergency window.
4) notify SRE and schedule postmortem.

alex: copying that into the runbook. also adding a gentle alarm: if NLB unhealthy > 10% within 10m, do immediate rollback.

samir: show me the plan output snippet for the route change?

alex: here's the relevant chunk:
```
# module.network.aws_lb_target_group_attachment.route: replace
-/resource: aws_lb_target_group_attachment.old
+/resource: aws_lb_target_group_attachment.new
~ aws_lb_target_group.group (will be updated)
```

mira: thanks. can we stagger apply so IAM first, then network? last time simultaneous caused config race on instance profile.

alex: good call. plan updated: run iam apply first (10m), verify, then network canary. deploy-bot will serialise.

deploy-bot: executing apply (step 1/2): module.iam. tracing logs -> https://deploy-logs.internal/tf-apply-20260320-01/iam

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: apply step 1/2 completed (iam). will wait 8m for verification then proceed with network canary.

(8m later)

deploy-bot: executing apply (step 2/2): module.network. canary traffic target=10%.

(3m into canary)

kyle: seeing NLB unhealthy host counts rising in datacenter-us-east-1:TG-42. 2/20 targets unhealthy.

ivy: logs show 504 gateway from new target group, health-checks failing on path /_health (200 expected).

alex: pause canary now and roll back network changes. deploy-bot pause.

deploy-bot: pausing run_id=tf-apply-20260320-01. canary halted at 10%.

alex: running emergency rollback script: `./scripts/rollback-network.sh tf-apply-20260320-01`

samir: command output:
```
Stopping canary traffic... OK
Reverting module.network -> v2.3.8... OK
Running targeted apply: terraform apply -target=module.network -var-file=rollback.tfvars -auto-approve
Apply complete. Restoring TG config... OK
```

ops-bot: health-check re-evaluation: TG-42 healthy=19/20 after rollback.

deploy-bot: run_id=tf-apply-20260320-01 marked FAILED->rolled-back. not reattempting network apply.

mira: good catch everyone. opening postmortem ticket and tagging SLO owners.

alex: notes for postmortem: flaky terratest route53 was ignored — add stricter gate. consider short-lived staging canary for network changes next time.

ivy: will add a checklist item: run NLB health-checks against new image in staging with identical TG config before prod canary.

kyle: thumbs up. can we schedule a dry-run apply next Thursday in the staging window?

alex: yes — scheduling dry-run and follow-up review doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:
